assist.exactQuestion: Acquire materially new primary or independent evidence reusable by the root owner to close source-addressed underwriting gaps.

claims.claim: Independent BTW analysis separates Varonis June 2026 SaaS ARR of $726.0M from SaaS ARR excluding conversions of $598.1M, calculating a $127.9M conversion layer (17.6% of total SaaS ARR). It also notes first-half free cash flow fell to $69.1M from $82.7M while SaaS revenue rose 62%.
claims.materiality: This independently constrains interpretation of headline SaaS growth: a material portion reflects migration of existing self-hosted contracts rather than purely new organic SaaS demand, while cash generation weakened during the transition. It is directly reusable by Alpha for confidence calibration without changing Alpha's numeric authority.

risks.risk: Headline SaaS ARR growth can overstate organic demand if conversion-driven ARR is not separated; transition economics remain sensitive to post-migration retention and cash conversion.

contradictions.statement: The independent analysis does not dispute Varonis's reported SaaS ARR, but shows that total SaaS ARR growth and organic SaaS growth describe different engines; treating the headline 52% growth as purely organic would be misleading.

unknowns: The eventual churn and realized economics of the remaining self-hosted cohort after the December 31, 2026 end-of-life remain uncertain.
This source does not independently establish customer-level satisfaction or competitive win/loss rates.
recommendedNextState: Reassess/confirm dataConfidence with this independent transition-quality constraint while preserving Alpha numeric underwriting authority.

learning.failedStrategy: Additional issuer/SEC repetition would not diversify the packet's confidence basis.
learning.changedStrategy: Changed source class to independent financial analysis and targeted the composition/quality of SaaS growth plus cash conversion rather than repeating issuer-reported headline growth.
learning.nextLawfulAction: Alpha should consume the independent conversion-layer and cash-flow evidence when deciding whether source diversity and uncertainty treatment now support closing dataConfidence.
